Galvanic corrosion occurs when two dissimilar metals are in direct electrical contact in the presence of an electrolyte (such as salt water).
claims.evidence: Galvanic corrosion (see Figure 1-7) occurs when different metals are in contact with each other and an electrolyte (such as salt water).

claims.claim: Galvanic corrosion is usually recognized by a buildup of corrosion at the joint between the metals.
claims.evidence: It is usually recognizable by a buildup of corrosion at the joint between the metals.

claims.claim: The less corrosion-resistant metal (higher in the galvanic series) becomes the anode and corrodes; the more corrosion-resistant metal becomes the cathode.
claims.evidence: The less corrosion-resistant metal (the higher metal in Figure 1-2) becomes the anode and the more corrosion- resistant metal (the lower metal in Figure 1-2) becomes the cathode.

claims.claim: The farther apart the metals are in the galvanic series, the more severe the anodic corrosion.
claims.evidence: The farther apart the metals are in Table 6-4, the more severe will be the corrosion of the anodic metal

claims.claim: A small anode in contact with a large cathode corrodes much more severely than a large anode in contact with a small cathode.
claims.evidence: A small anode in contact with a large cathode will corrode much more severely than a large anode in contact with a small cathode.

claims.claim: The galvanic series is a good predictor of how a couple will corrode.
claims.evidence: In most cases, the galvanic series listed in Table 6-4 is a good predictor of how metals will corrode in a galvanic couple.

claims.claim: Filiform corrosion is an oxygen concentration cell (crevice-type) corrosion on surfaces with an organic coating.
claims.evidence: Filiform corrosion is a special form of oxygen concentration cell corrosion (or crevice corrosion) that occurs on metal surfaces having an organic coating system.

claims.claim: Filiform corrosion shows as wormlike corrosion-product traces under the paint.
claims.evidence: It is recognizable by its characteristic wormlike trace of corrosion products beneath the paint film

claims.claim: Filiform corrosion starts at breaks in the coating (scratches, cracks around fasteners and seams).
claims.evidence: It starts at breaks in the coating system (such as scratches and cracks around fasteners and seams)

claims.claim: Filiform corrosion occurs at relative humidity of about 78–90% on slightly acidic surfaces.
claims.evidence: Filiform occurs when the relative humidity of the air is between 78 and 90%, and when the surface is slightly acidic.

claims.claim: Filiform corrosion can attack steel, magnesium, and aluminum.
claims.evidence: Filiform corrosion can attack steel, magnesium, and aluminum surfaces

claims.claim: Prevention: store equipment and aircraft in an environment with relative humidity below 70%.
claims.evidence: Filiform corrosion can be prevented by storing equipment and aircraft in an environment with a relative humidity below 70%

claims.claim: Prevention: use coating systems having a low rate of diffusion for oxygen and water vapor.
claims.evidence: by using coating systems having a low rate of diffusion for oxygen and water vapors

claims.claim: Prevention: maintain coatings in good condition and promptly touch up paint damage, especially around fasteners.
claims.evidence: Maintain coatings in good condition (prompt touch-up around fasteners)

claims.claim: Prevention: wash equipment and aircraft to remove acidic contaminants (e.g., air pollutants).
claims.evidence: washing equipment and aircraft to remove acidic contaminants from the surface (such as those created by pollutants in the air)

claims.claim: Prevention: apply corrosion preventive compounds (CPCs) where paint is damaged.
claims.evidence: apply corrosion preventive compounds (CPC's) when paint is damaged.

claims.claim: TO 35-1-3 and TO 1-1-691 give the same prevention measures; TO 1-1-691 also specifies the CPC step.
claims.evidence: Filiform corrosion can be prevented by: storing equipment in an environ- ment with a relative humidity below 70 percent; using coating systems with a low rate of diffusion

claims.claim: The galvanic corrosion points are supported by TO 1-1-700.
claims.evidence: the rate at which corrosion occurs depends on the difference in their chemical activities, that is, their positions in the galvanic series (see Figure 3-17). The greater the difference in activity, the faster corrosion occurs.
